newsitem.title: USA: UAL "sorry" pilots reject wage offer.
newsitem.headline: UAL "sorry" pilots reject wage offer.

text.p: United Airlines said Thursday it is sorry the Air Line Pilots Association rejected a wage proposal and will have to submit to binding arbitration.
"I am very sorry to report that United's pilots have rejected the mid-term wage agreement," said Gerald Greenwald, United chief executive officer, in a statement.
"The vote was about 80 percent against the agreement. Under the terms of the company's 1994 agreement with ALPA, the issue is now subject to outside, independent arbitration," he said.

The vote centered on a wage adjustment which was included as a provision of the pilots July 1994 employee-ownership agreement (ESOP). United's employees own 55 percent of the its common stock. United is a subsidiary of UAL Corp.
